records.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset: ONE new AITI souvenir-card character action illustration, not a card mockup.
Canvas: 1024 x 1536 PNG, vertical 2:3, pure opaque white background. ONE complete character in ONE pose; all extremities and the specified props visible, with comfortable margins and generous clean whitespace. No four-view layout, inset, border, room, floor shadow, watermark, signature, model title or extra character.
Rendering for this first action draft: refined 2D Japanese light illustration, very fine clean dark grey-brown/colored lines, restrained pastel/desaturated colors, subtle cel shading, clean smoothly colored shapes and crisp intentional highlights, soft upper-left light. Match the referenced sheets' finish across this series. No 3D/clay/plastic render, photorealism, pixel art, thick black outline, heavy paint, watercolor bleed or muddy/mottled blur.
The reference sheet establishes identity, anatomy, proportions, colors and physical accessory placement, NOT the output layout or neutral pose. Re-illustrate the approved new action. Do not copy FRONT/LEFT/BACK/RIGHT labels or any other sheet lettering. Preserve the complete species-appropriate body; no new appendages.

INPUT REFERENCES:
Image 1: authoritative character identity and anatomy.
Image 2: series fine-line rendering reference only.

Identity: the complete QUADRUPED snowy-white dragon in Image 1: four clawed feet, small pale-lavender membrane wings, two ivory segmented horns, one long scaled tapering tail, purple serious eyes. Action: low crouch on all four legs, one front claw resting flat on an unfolded plan sheet. Lower the head close to ONE small schematic fault near a corner of the paper, eyes narrowed in meticulous concentration; bend the tail forward so its tapered tip indicates that same fault. Show a clear relationship among gaze, paper, front claw and tail tip. Three-quarter front view, with the face and identifying horn charm readable. Match their keycap footprint, bevel, height and regular row/column spacing. Its base must sit naturally inside the keyboard, with a small believable contact shadow; no floating, rotated, stacked, overhanging or intersecting cap. Remove the old displaced edge and repair only the tiny exposed area immediately around it. The paw should still visibly rest on the corrected purple top.

Preserve both paws' locations, tired blue-grey eyes, face, fur strands, forehead sleep mask, tail, body proportions and pose. Preserve the monitor, other keycaps, keyboard case, framing, pure white background, original fine line quality, original colors, soft shadows and every highlight. Keep all image pixels outside this tiny keycap correction as close to the original as possible.
